title: SLO-driven rate limit fallbacks — UX notes & backlog
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures UX hypotheses, wireframe directions, and a prioritised backlog for exposing SLO-driven rate-limit fallbacks in the Console. The focus is on per-key and per-route breakdowns so developers can debug, configure, and recover from quota events with minimal support involvement.

Goals:
- Surface why a request was throttled (SLO hit, quota exhaustion, burst control) at the credential and route level.
- Offer fast remediation: temporary bypass, emergency capacity request, priority lane assignment.
- Make fallback behavior observable and reversible (audit + timeline).
- Help product/infra decide default fallback policies and expose safe overrides.

Primary personas and jobs-to-be-done:
- Platform engineer: wants to diagnose tenant outages and assign temporary capacity to high-priority keys.
- App developer: wants clear guidance when their routes are being limited and a one-click path to request more headroom.
- Support engineer: wants a read-only timeline plus quick actions to route traffic to a lower-cost compatible model variant.

User stories (examples):
- As an app developer, I want to see a timeline for my API key showing spikes, SLO triggers, and which routes were throttled so I can correlate to deploys.
- As a platform engineer, I want to temporarily elevate a key to a priority lane for 30 minutes during an incident and have the action logged.
- As SRE, I want the UI to recommend a fallback (model variant, increased burst quota, caching) based on traffic shape.

Wireframe/interaction notes (surface-level descriptions for design):
1) Credential Overview panel (top-level)
- Compact summary: current quota vs committed capacity, active SLOs, recent throttle events count.
- Quick-actions: Request temporary capacity, Attach priority-lane, View incident timeline.

2) Per-route breakdown view (expand from credential)
- Left column: list of routes with sparkline indicating throttle frequency and median p95 latency.
- Center: selected route timeline with layered lanes for: token consumption, SLO threshold (configurable), throttle windows, fallback activations. Color-coding: green (within SLO), amber (approaching), red (throttled).
- Right column: suggested mitigations (auto-batching, quantization suggestion, fallback model) with estimated cost delta +/- percent.

3) Throttle event detail modal
- Top: offending request example (redacted), route, key, timestamp, tokens in request, SLO snapshot at that time.
- Middle: root-cause classifier (heuristic): sudden traffic spike | sustained rate | KV cache miss storms | downstream slow responses.
- Bottom: actions: Open support ticket (prefilled), Grant temporary burst (30m/2h), Apply automatic fallback to cheaper model (with show/undo).

Backlog (prioritised, with rough effort and acceptance criteria):
- BL-1: Add per-key timeline widget (MVP) — effort: 3 team-weeks. Acceptance: shows token consumption, throttle markers, supports 7 days of zoom.
- BL-2: Throttle detail modal + root-cause tags — effort: 2 weeks. Acceptance: modal links to example requests and suggests mitigation.
- BL-3: One-click temporary priority lane (audit logging) — effort: 1 week (safety review required). Acceptance: action available to owners, creates audit row and auto-expiry.
- BL-4: Suggested mitigation engine (UI surface) — effort: 4 weeks (ML/heuristic dev + UX). Acceptance: returns at least 3 ranked suggestions with cost delta estimates.
- BL-5: Per-route cost delta preview (charge simulation) — effort: 2 weeks. Acceptance: shows estimated monthly cost impact for enabling fallback.

Data & metrics to surface (backend contract notes):
- time-series: tokens_consumed, requests, errors, p50/p95 latency, throttle_count (by reason), fallback_active(Boolean).
- metadata: credential_id, route_name, model_variant, region, site_tier.
- audit events: action, actor_id, timestamp, expiry.

Edge cases & safety notes:
- Emergency bypass must be rate-limited and gated by roles. UI must show explicit warnings and require 2-step confirmation for >2h overrides.
- When suggesting fallback to cheaper model, include a quality guidance note (expected degradation probability %) and link to evals.
- Avoid exposing raw request payloads in shared views; only show redacted snippets.

Open questions for PM/Infra: (for grooming)
- What are allowed default fallback variants per customer tier? (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- How do we compute cost-delta estimates for mixed-quantization models?
- Should automatic fallbacks be enabled by default for self-serve users?

Design experiments (A/B):
- A: Show mitigation suggestions inline on throttle markers vs B: separate recommendations panel. Measure time-to-remediate and number of support tickets opened.

Next steps & owners: 
- Design: produce 2 mid-fidelity mocks for the Credential Overview and Throttle Modal (owner: Leah). Due: 2026-03-12.
- Data/instrumentation: contract for additional time-series and throttle-reason tags (owner: Marco). Due: 2026-03-05.
- Infra/authorization: draft flow for temporary priority lane with audit schema (owner: Samir). Due: 2026-03-19.

Notes / working thoughts (quick brain dump):
- Consider adding a "playback" feature that replays timeline at accelerated speed highlighting when fallback flipped on/off. Helpful for postmortems.
- For the per-route view, allow saving a "debug filter" (range + route + key + model) to reproduce later.
- Think about mapping throttle reasons to Slack alert templates for SRE on-call.

This doc is intentionally high-level to seed design work and backlog grooming. Add comments below with specific UX constraints, or paste screenshots/mock links.
